facts: N. Bhargavan Pillai (Dead) By Lrs.And Anr. v State Of Kerala
The accused was employed in the Civil Supplies Department in the rank of Assistant Taluk Supply Officer.
He was working as Junior Manager on deputation in the Kerala State Civil Supplies Corporation (in short the 'Corporation'), at Kowdiar.
Pursuant to the orders he took charge as Unit Manager in the Punalur Unit.
His 5 years deputation to the Corporation was to be completed on 30.6.1986.
But, instead of relieving him, the Corporation had requested the Civil Supplies Department to extend his term of deputation by one year stating that certain liabilities were outstanding.
The accused did not hand over charge on 29.11.1986.
He did not attend the office after 27.11.1986, but applied for leave.

As he did not attend the office on 29.11.1986, the Regional Manager by Ext.P-22 dated 1.12.1986 permitted Natarajan Asari (PW-3), the Senior Assistant in the Punalur depot to assume charge effective from that date.
issues: Whether the whole proceeding was non est and the trial was vitiated in the absence of a sanction for the prosecution in terms of Section 19 of the Act and Section 197 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short the 'Code')
Whether the prosecution has established any mis-appropriation and/or mens rea of the alleged crime
petitioner_arguments: In the absence of a sanction for the prosecution in terms of Section 19 of the Act and Section 197 of the Code, the whole proceeding was non est and the trial was vitiated
The prosecution has not established any mis-appropriation and/or mens rea of the alleged crime
Both the trial Court and the High Court proceeded on mere surmises and conjectures to hold that the accused had committed mis- appropriation
The essential ingredients necessary to prove the accusations under Section 409 IPC are squarely absent
Even if the accused had agreed to pay the amount, that was not material while considering the issue whether the ingredients have been established by the prosecution
respondent_arguments: The Courts below have acted in accordance with law keeping in view the correct principles and the factual scenario
Mis- appropriation is no part of an employee's official duty and, therefore, the question of any sanction under Section 197 of the Code does not arise
Initially, the sanction was not accorded because the accused had retired and had agreed to pay the amount but that was not the final decision
In a case involving corruption it would be against public interest not to proceed against the accused who is guilty of mis-appopriating huge amount of stock meant for the people
court_reasoning: The Courts below have acted in accordance with law keeping in view the correct principles and the factual scenario
Mis- appropriation is no part of an employee's official duty and, therefore, the question of any sanction under Section 197 of the Code does not arise
holding: The conviction and sentence are confirmed
